itens.t: Russian Warship Sinks Off Libya After Suspected Ukrainian Strikes
itens.r: A Russian warship capsized and sank after suspected Ukrainian sea drones struck a naval base in eastern Libya. The attack triggered a massive explosion and subsequent fire at the facility, according to local Libyan officials. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy later claimed direct responsibility for the operation, marking a significant expansion of the conflict beyond the Black Sea. Hours following the initial strike, a second drone attack further targeted naval assets in the region.
itens.d:
A Russian warship capsized and sank Sunday after suspected Ukrainian sea drones struck a naval base in eastern Libya, triggering an explosion and fire, according to Libyan officials. Hours later, a second drone attack also hit a commercial ship off the coast of Benghazi.

The first ship, the Russian navy corvette Merkury, was docked at Benghazi Naval Base when two explosive-laden sea drones struck the vessel. Ten people suffered minor injuries in the attack and received treatment in Benghazi. Officials stated the warship had stopped at the port to refuel and resupply while returning to Russia.
itens.e:
A Russian navy corvette, the Merkury, capsized and sank after being struck by suspected Ukrainian sea drones at a naval base in eastern Libya, where it had stopped to refuel and resupply. A subsequent drone attack later struck a commercial ship off the coast of Benghazi, resulting in ten minor injuries among personnel.

This incident highlights the expanding geographic scope of the conflict beyond traditional frontlines, directly impacting international port security and naval logistics in North Africa. The strikes affect Russian military transit capabilities as well as commercial shipping operations in Libyan waters, raising immediate concerns over regional stability.

One risk is that such maritime attacks could prompt broader security measures across Mediterranean ports. Observers should monitor whether further naval assets are targeted in foreign harbors and how Libyan officials respond to these security breaches.

itens.t: South Korea's President Lee Reshuffles Cabinet and Appoints First Female Spy Chief
itens.r: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung nominated a new foreign minister, three other cabinet ministers, and a new head for the national intelligence agency. Former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil was selected to lead the National Intelligence Service, making history as the country's first female spy chief.
itens.d:
South Korea's President Lee Jae Myung on Monday named a presidential cabinet reshuffle and appointed the country's first female spy chief.

The announcement was reported by Yonhap from Seoul, detailing the latest changes made by the administration.
itens.e:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung announced a comprehensive cabinet reshuffle, which notably included the appointment of the country's first female spy chief. The official announcement regarding these administrative changes was detailed from Seoul by Yonhap.

This restructuring matters significantly for the direction of national security and governance in South Korea, directly involving executive leadership and intelligence oversight. The historic appointment of a female intelligence chief marks a notable shift in the upper echelons of the nation's security apparatus, affecting how domestic and foreign policies may be coordinated moving forward.

Observers will need to watch for the formal confirmation and inauguration of the newly appointed officials, as well as any subsequent policy shifts. It remains to be seen how this restructured cabinet will address pressing domestic and international priorities under President Lee's administration.

itens.t: SpaceX Launches Two Rockets from Same Pad 32 Hours Apart, Smashing Record
itens.r: SpaceX set a new turnaround record by launching two Falcon 9 rockets from the same California pad just 32 hours apart.
itens.d:
SpaceX set a new record with its latest satellite launch out of California when a Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base on Sunday. The mission carried out a payload for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office called NROL-136.

This launch occurred just over 32 hours after a previous liftoff from the same pad for the U.S. Space Force, smashing the previous turnaround record of 45 hours set at Pad 40 in Florida. Kiko Dontchev, SpaceX's vice president of launch, highlighted the achievement on X.
itens.e:
SpaceX achieved a new turnaround record by launching a Falcon 9 rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California just over 32 hours after a previous liftoff from the same pad. The mission successfully carried the NROL-136 payload for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office, following a prior launch for the U.S. Space Force.

This rapid operational tempo demonstrates significant advancements in launch frequency and pad efficiency, a milestone highlighted by SpaceX vice president of launch Kiko Dontchev. The capability directly benefits defense and intelligence agencies by enabling faster deployment schedules for critical national security payloads.

One risk is maintaining this high cadence without compromising safety or vehicle reliability. Observers should watch whether SpaceX can consistently sustain or further shorten these turnaround intervals across its various launch sites in future missions.

itens.t: Major US Financial Institutions Ban Third-Party AI Bots from Bank Accounts
itens.r: Major US banks are cracking down on third-party AI agents logging into customer accounts, warning users that bot-related errors are their own responsibility.
itens.d:
Major US financial institutions are banning third-party bots from logging into user bank accounts. They are also warning that any costly bot mistakes are strictly the responsibility of the account holders.

The new restrictions highlight growing security and operational concerns surrounding automated tools accessing financial platforms.

itens.t: Rayssa Leal Wins Gold at World Skateboarding Championship in Japan
itens.r: Brazilian skater Rayssa Leal scored 176.03 points in Utsunomiya to secure the street skateboarding title over strong Olympic competition.
itens.d:
Rayssa Leal won the gold medal at the street skateboarding World Cup stage in Utsunomiya, Japan, scoring 176,03 points. Australia's Chloe Covell took silver with 175,13 points, while Olympic champion Coco Yoshizawa finished third with 175,11 points.

The victory earned the 18-year-old Brazilian 50,000 points in the world ranking, concluding the first qualifying phase for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games. In the men's competition, fellow Brazilian Sebastian Simonetto finished in eighth place with 136,71 points.

itens.t: VIDEO: Musk Just Revealed Starship V4, and It Changes Everything
itens.r: A detailed technical breakdown of SpaceX's Starship V4 reveal and the ongoing work on Ship 42's heat shield tiles.
itens.d:
The video covers the return of SpaceX's Ship 42 and examines a failed heat shield tile among 18,000 during descent. It discusses why a steel rocket appears rainbow-colored due to tower arms scraping black dust off the hull, and highlights a 1974 NASA helicopter idea used as a fix.

Additionally, the presentation features statements from Elon Musk regarding the upcoming Starship v4 upper stage, cost estimates for filling the rocket, and details about future launch locations between Texas and Florida.

itens.t: Russian Drone Attack on Apartment Building in Kyiv Region Kills 11
itens.r: At least eleven people were killed in a Russian drone strike on a residential apartment building in Dymer.
itens.d:
At least 11 people died in a Russian drone attack against a multi-story residential building in Dymer, in the Kyiv region, while a young boy and an elderly woman were rescued alive from the rubble. The Ukrainian Air Force reported that 153 drones were launched starting Sunday evening, with 134 intercepted by air defenses.

Rescue teams worked overnight searching for survivors, recovering 11 bodies from the destroyed building. A 7-year-old boy named David was pulled alive after spending nearly 14 hours under the debris, and a 79-year-old woman named Valentyna was rescued after 22 hours trapped under concrete.

itens.t: Kim Jong Un Personally Receives Foreign Ambassadors' Credentials
itens.r: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un personally accepted diplomatic credentials for the first time, stating Pyongyang's foreign policy seeks neither supremacy nor expansion.
itens.d:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un personally accepted the credentials of newly appointed ambassadors for the first time on Sunday. He told the envoys that Pyongyang's foreign policy neither pursues supremacy nor expansion.

The Korean Central News Agency reported Monday that Kim received diplomats representing ten different countries, including Russia, Sweden, Indonesia, Vietnam, Brazil, and the Czech Republic.

itens.t: Biologically Important Chemical Reactions Persist in Sterilized Soil for Six Years
itens.r: Scientists discovered that biological chemical reactions can persist in sterilized dirt for years, offering clues about the origins of life on Earth.
itens.d:
Biologically important chemical reactions persisted in sterilized soil for six years, according to findings discussed in recent reports. This persistence offers new clues regarding how life on Earth may have originally begun.

The research provides insights into chemical stability and potential prebiotic processes under sterile conditions.

itens.t: Copyright Battle Over Artificial Intelligence Tests Legal Principles in US
itens.r: A major legal showdown between news organizations and artificial intelligence developers is testing traditional copyright laws under the current administration.
itens.d:
A major court battle is testing copyright principles as several news organizations, including The New York Times, sue OpenAI and Microsoft for using millions of articles to train artificial intelligence systems. The newspapers argue this violates copyright protections, while tech firms contend it qualifies as fair use.

The Department of Justice has sided with OpenAI, filing a statement of interest that embraces an expansive vision of fair use. Critics argue this interpretation threatens to turn a narrow exception into a blanket exemption, potentially harming creators while lowering costs for AI developers.

itens.d:
Alcaraz dominated Zverev to capture his maiden ATP Finals title. With this victory, he joined an exclusive list of men who have won all four major tournaments and the ATP Finals.

The triumph cements his status among the elite players in tennis history.

itens.t: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro Remains in ICU with Stable Condition
itens.r: Ex-president Jair Bolsonaro continues recovering in a Brasília intensive care unit while remaining clinically stable with no discharge date set.
itens.d:
Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro remains hospitalized in an intensive care unit in Brasília in a clinically stable condition with no discharge date set, according to a medical bulletin released Sunday afternoon. He has been hospitalized since Friday after experiencing severe stomach pain and being diagnosed with acute obstructive abdomen.

His cardiologist, Brasil Ramos Caiado, recommended the transfer from house arrest for specialized evaluation. Medical treatment includes hydration, fasting, nutritional support, and a gastric tube, while doctors have not ruled out the possibility of a new surgery.

itens.t: South Korea's Exports Forecast to Exceed $1 Trillion for Second Straight Year
itens.r: Strong global semiconductor demand is projected to keep South Korean exports above the trillion-dollar mark through 2027.
itens.d:
South Korea's exports are expected to exceed $1 trillion for the second consecutive year in 2027, driven by global demand for semiconductors, according to a state-run think tank. The Korea Institute for Industrial Economics & Trade forecast exports to reach $1.32 trillion, up 14.1 percent from this year's estimate.

The trade surplus is projected to rise to $455.9 billion next year, with the economy expected to grow by 3.5 percent. However, the institute highlighted downside risks including uncertainties over U.S. trade policies and conflicts in the Middle East.

itens.t: US Senator Warns North Korea Growing More Lethal Due to Ukraine War
itens.r: A prominent US senator cautioned that North Korea's military cooperation with Russia is significantly enhancing its combat capabilities.
itens.d:
North Korea's deployment of troops to support Russia's war against Ukraine is turning the country into a more capable military threat, a prominent U.S. senator has warned. The official argued that this cooperation will constrain Washington's freedom to act.

Democratic Senator Chris Coons of Delaware made the remarks while speaking at the Halifax International Security Forum over the weekend.

itens.t: Director Jonathan Frakes Reflects on 30th Anniversary of Star Trek: First Contact
itens.r: Director Jonathan Frakes discusses the enduring legacy of the sci-fi classic as the film reaches its 30th milestone.
itens.d:
Star Trek: First Contact celebrates its 30th anniversary, remaining a widely praised science fiction classic directed by Jonathan Frakes in his feature film debut. Released by Paramount over Thanksgiving week in 1996, the movie was both a financial success and a crowd-pleaser, grossing $212 million worldwide.

In reflections on the milestone, director Jonathan Frakes discussed the lasting appeal of the screenplay by Brannon Braga and Ronald D. Moore, as well as memorable performances by the cast including Patrick Stewart, Alice Krige, and Brent Spiner.

itens.t: Super El Niño Weather Phenomenon Threatens to Worsen Global Food Security
itens.r: Meteorological shifts are combining with regional droughts and conflicts to place millions of vulnerable people at risk of hunger.
itens.d:
The super El Niño weather phenomenon threatens to worsen global food security by causing massive droughts in some regions while bringing excessive rain to others. Combined with ongoing conflicts and foreign aid cuts, these weather patterns could leave millions in vulnerable countries without sufficient food.

The compounding crises raise serious concerns for international humanitarian efforts and agricultural stability.

itens.t: Brazilian Chamber of Deputies Weighs Government Fiscal Adjustment Package
itens.r: Lawmakers in Brazil's lower house have begun evaluating a critical fiscal adjustment proposal aimed at reining in public expenditures.
itens.d:
A Câmara dos Deputados analisa nesta segunda-feira a proposta de ajuste fiscal do governo, com o relator Mauro Benevides mantendo o texto aprovado pelo Senado. O projeto altera o arcabouço fiscal para dar ao governo ferramentas de controle das contas públicas, com um impacto estimado em R$ 50 bilhões em 2027.

Economistas apontam que a medida representa um avanço inicial limitado, correspondendo a cerca de 0,3% do PIB, e que novas propostas estruturais serão necessárias para controlar a dívida pública. O valor final do ajuste sofreu revisão para baixo em relação aos cálculos iniciais feitos pelo Senado.

itens.d:

The report highlights the profound long-term hazards affecting living conditions and ecological safety in the region.

itens.t: SK Group Chairman Offers Record Settlement to End Nine-Year Divorce Dispute
itens.r: The head of South Korea's SK Group has agreed to pay a multi-billion won settlement to conclude a lengthy high-profile divorce battle.
itens.d:
SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won has offered to pay his former wife, Art Center Nabi Director Roh So-young, the full 944 billion won awarded in their divorce settlement. The move seeks to end a nearly decade-long legal battle over marital assets.

Chey asked the Supreme Court to recommend a settlement based on the latest appellate court ruling, which would make the agreement legally binding under South Korean law.

The victory cements Marquez's legacy as one of the most dominant riders in the sport's history.

itens.t: Amazon Launches New Batch of Internet Satellites Following Recent Failure
itens.r: Amazon deployed its latest constellation of internet satellites aboard an Ariane 6 rocket following a previous launch setback.
itens.d:
Amazon is scheduled to launch a new batch of internet satellites using an Ariane 6 rocket from French Guiana, just eight days after a launch failure doomed 40 spacecraft. The mission will carry 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation into low Earth orbit.

The Amazon Leo network aims to eventually deploy over 3,200 satellites to compete with SpaceX's Starlink constellation. The previous satellite loss occurred on November 15 during a flight using a United Launch Alliance Vulcan Centaur rocket, which is currently grounded for investigation.

itens.d:
Ruling Democratic Party of Korea Chairman Kim Min-seok faces factional feuds and leadership tests as he reaches his 100th day in office. Public support for the party has slipped to 36 percent in a Gallup Korea poll, down from 41 percent before he took office.

Kim's leadership faces additional strain as party hard-liners push to impeach Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae, a move that risks alienating moderate voters and testing his ability to unify the party.

itens.r: Market projections indicate that Brazil will significantly increase its foreign purchases of anhydrous ethanol heading into early 2027.
itens.d:
O Brasil deve importar cerca de 562 milhões de litros de etanol anidro entre janeiro e março de 2027, o que representa um aumento de 59% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior. A projeção da StoneX aponta que a redução dos estoques no Centro-Sul e o crescimento da demanda motivam as compras externas.

Os estoques na região caíram para 2,85 bilhões de litros, o menor volume para o período desde a safra 2021/22. Além disso, a elevação da mistura obrigatória de etanol na gasolina para 32% ampliou a pressão sobre a oferta interna.

The strong financial performance was driven by sales of higher-value substrates designed for artificial intelligence data centers, pushing Samsung's operating margin to 15.2 percent.

O clube planeja usar a equipe de base nas primeiras rodadas do Campeonato Carioca para preservar os titulares. Além disso, a diretoria estuda realizar uma intertemporada na Europa, com preferência por Portugal, antes do início das principais competições do ano.

The student-led advocacy group organized two rounds of signature campaigns following student confusion during the CSAT.

The controversy emerged after the top scorer on a certified tax accountant exam admitted to cheating using miniature technology and generative AI. The petitioners are demanding clearer procedures for appeals and score invalidation criteria from the Ministry of Education.
